```{r}
library(lme4)
library(emmeans)
library(performance)
```


```{r}
d <- read.csv('comparative_long.csv')

d$participant <- factor(d$participant)
d$dataset     <- factor(d$dataset)
d$item        <- factor(d$item)
```

Let's just do the Telco analysis first
```{r}
d_telco <- subset(d, dataset == "telco")

ctrl <- glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")

# Telco: full model (just participant because of singularity)
m_telco_full <- glmer(choice ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
                      data = d_telco, family = binomial, control = ctrl)

# Singularity check (TRUE = singular)
isSingular(m_telco_full)

# Variance components (item variance near 0 = cause of singularity)
VarCorr(m_telco_full)

# Fixed effects
summary(m_telco_full)

#ICC of models
icc(m_telco_full)

#Confidence Intervals
confint(m_telco_full)
```

```{r}
d_med   <- subset(d, dataset == "medical")

ctrl <- glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")

# Medical: full model (participant + item)
m_med_full <- glmer(choice ~ 1 + (1 | participant) + (1 | item),
                    data = d_med, family = binomial, control = ctrl)

# Singularity check (TRUE = singular)
isSingular(m_med_full)

# Variance components (item variance near 0 = cause of singularity)
VarCorr(m_med_full)

# Fixed effects
summary(m_med_full)

#ICC of models
icc(m_med_full, by_group = TRUE)

#Confidence Intervals
confint(m_med_full)
```
```{r}
#Get back-transformed rations
cc <- confint(m_telco_full, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald") # Wald method is fastest
ctab <- cbind(Estimate = fixef(m_telco_full), cc)

# 3. Exponentiate to get Odds Ratios and 95% CIs
exp_table <- exp(ctab)
print(exp_table)
```

```{r}
#Get back-transformed rations
cc <- confint(m_med_full, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald") # Wald method is fastest
ctab <- cbind(Estimate = fixef(m_med_full), cc)

# 3. Exponentiate to get Odds Ratios and 95% CIs
exp_table <- exp(ctab)
print(exp_table)
```


```{r}
library(lme4)

# --- Helper: back-transform a glmer intercept-only (or +item) model ---
report_intercept <- function(model, ci_method = c("wald", "profile")) {
  ci_method <- match.arg(ci_method)

  est <- fixef(model)[["(Intercept)"]]
  se  <- sqrt(vcov(model)[1, 1])

  if (ci_method == "wald") {
    ci_logit <- est + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se
  } else {
    ci_logit <- confint(model, method = "profile", parm = "(Intercept)")
  }

  data.frame(
    estimate   = est,
    se         = se,
    z          = est / se,
    p          = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)),
    OR         = exp(est),
    OR_lo      = exp(ci_logit[1]),
    OR_hi      = exp(ci_logit[2]),
    prob       = plogis(est),
    prob_lo    = plogis(ci_logit[1]),
    prob_hi    = plogis(ci_logit[2])
  )
}

# --- Fit the two models as specified (telco: participant only; medical: + prototype) ---
ctrl <- glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")

m_telco <- glmer(choice ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
                 data = subset(d, dataset == "telco"),
                 family = binomial, control = ctrl)

m_med <- glmer(choice ~ 1 + (1 | participant) + (1 | item),
              data = subset(d, dataset == "medical"),
              family = binomial, control = ctrl)

# --- Reportable estimates (Wald CI, matching your table) ---
telco_out <- report_intercept(m_telco, "wald")
med_out   <- report_intercept(m_med, "wald")

round(rbind(telco = telco_out, medical = med_out), 3)
```

Let's check assumptions
```{r}
library(lme4)
library(DHARMa)
library(influence.ME)

res_telco <- simulateResiduals(m_telco, n = 1000, seed = 123)
res_med   <- simulateResiduals(m_med,   n = 1000, seed = 123)

plot(res_telco)     # QQ plot plus residual-vs-predicted

testUniformity(res_telco)           # KS test: overall distribution
testOutliers(res_telco)
testDispersion(res_telco)           # reported for completeness; uninformative for Bernoulli
```
Repeat for Med
```{r}
plot(res_med) 

testUniformity(res_med)           # KS test: overall distribution
testOutliers(res_med)
testDispersion(res_med)           # reported for completeness; uninformative for Bernoulli
```
```{r}
res_telco_p <- recalculateResiduals(res_telco, group = d_telco$participant)
testUniformity(res_telco_p)
plot(res_telco_p)

res_med_p <- recalculateResiduals(res_med, group = d_med$participant)
testUniformity(res_med_p)
plot(res_med_p)
```
Normality of random intercepts
```{r}
re_p <- ranef(m_telco)$participant[, 1]
qqnorm(re_p); qqline(re_p)
shapiro.test(re_p)

re_p_med <- ranef(m_med)$participant[, 1]
re_i_med <- ranef(m_med)$item[, 1]
qqnorm(re_p_med); qqline(re_p_med)
shapiro.test(re_p_med)
# items: only 10 levels, so interpret visually and cautiously
```

```{r}
loo <- sapply(unique(d_med$participant), function(p) {
  m <- update(m_med, data = subset(d_med, participant != p))
  fixef(m)[1]
})
range(loo)   # should stay clearly above 0
```

```{r}
loo <- sapply(unique(d_telco$participant), function(p) {
  m <- update(m_telco, data = subset(d_telco, participant != p))
  fixef(m)[1]
})
range(loo)   # should stay clearly above 0
```

```{r}
isSingular(m_telco); isSingular(m_med)
m_med@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages     # NULL = no convergence warnings

# Laplace approximation can be biased with few trials per cluster (here 5).
# Compare with adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (single random effect only):
m_telco_agq <- update(m_telco, nAGQ = 10)
cbind(laplace = fixef(m_telco), agq = fixef(m_telco_agq))
```
```{r}
library(glmmTMB)
m_med_tmb <- glmmTMB(choice ~ 1 + (1 | participant) + (1 | item),
                     data = d_med, family = binomial)
summary(m_med_tmb)
```
